questions.question: Which country won the 2022 FIFA World Cup held in Qatar?
questions.explanation: Argentina defeated France in a thrilling final that ended 3-3 after extra time, winning 4-2 on penalties.
questions.fact: This was Argentina's third World Cup title, and Lionel Messi's first.
questions.expected_discussion: Discuss Messi's legacy and the intensity of the final match.

questions.question: How many teams will participate in the 2026 FIFA World Cup?
questions.explanation: The 2026 edition will be the first to feature 48 teams, expanded from the traditional 32.
questions.fact: This expansion means there will be 104 matches in total during the tournament.
questions.expected_discussion: Talk about the impact of more teams on the tournament's length and global reach.

questions.question: Who won the Golden Boot award for scoring the most goals (8) in the 2022 FIFA World Cup?
questions.explanation: Kylian Mbappé scored a hat-trick in the final, bringing his tournament total to 8 goals.
questions.fact: He became only the second player ever to score a hat-trick in a World Cup final, after Geoff Hurst in 1966.
questions.expected_discussion: Discuss Mbappé's performance in the final and his future potential.

questions.question: True or False: The first-ever FIFA World Cup was held in 1930 and hosted by Uruguay.
questions.explanation: The inaugural tournament took place in Uruguay from 13 to 30 July 1930.
questions.fact: Uruguay also won the first tournament, defeating Argentina 4-2 in the final.
questions.expected_discussion: Mention how travel was difficult for European teams back in 1930.

questions.question: Which three countries will jointly host the 2026 FIFA World Cup?
questions.explanation: The 2026 FIFA World Cup will be hosted by 16 cities across these three North American nations.
questions.fact: Mexico will become the first country to host or co-host the men's World Cup three times (1970, 1986, 2026).
questions.expected_discussion: Discuss the logistics of hosting a tournament across three large countries.

questions.question: What is the official mascot of the Paris 2024 Olympic Games?
questions.explanation: The Phryges (Phrygian caps) are symbols of liberty in French history.
questions.fact: The design is based on the traditional small hats that are a symbol of freedom in France.
questions.expected_discussion: Explain the symbolism of the Phrygian cap in the French Revolution.

questions.question: Who is the most decorated Olympian of all time, with a total of 28 medals, including 23 gold?
questions.explanation: American swimmer Michael Phelps holds the record for most Olympic gold medals and most total medals.
questions.fact: He has more gold medals than 161 countries have won in their entire Olympic history.
questions.expected_discussion: Discuss the physical and mental discipline required to sustain such a career.

questions.question: What do the five rings on the Olympic flag represent?
questions.answer: The five continents of the world
options: The five continents of the world
questions.explanation: The rings represent Africa, the Americas, Asia, Europe, and Oceania.
questions.fact: The colors (Blue, Yellow, Black, Green, Red) were chosen because every national flag in the world contains at least one of them.
questions.expected_discussion: Emphasize the theme of global unity through sports.

questions.question: Which city will host the 2028 Summer Olympic Games?
questions.explanation: Los Angeles was selected to host the 2028 Games, marking the third time the city hosts the Olympics (1932, 1984).
questions.fact: LA will join London and Paris as the only cities to have hosted the Summer Games three times.
questions.expected_discussion: Talk about LA's iconic sporting venues like the Coliseum.

questions.question: What is the updated Olympic motto, which now includes the word 'Together'?
questions.explanation: In 2021, the IOC approved adding 'Communiter' (Together) to the original motto 'Faster, Higher, Stronger'.
questions.fact: The update was made to recognize the unifying power of sport and the importance of solidarity.
questions.expected_discussion: Discuss why 'Together' was added in the post-pandemic context.

questions.question: Identify this Indian athlete who won Gold at Tokyo 2020 and Silver at Paris 2024 in Javelin Throw.
questions.explanation: Neeraj Chopra is the first Indian track and field athlete to win an Olympic gold medal.
questions.fact: His gold medal in Tokyo was India's first ever Olympic gold in athletics.
questions.expected_discussion: Discuss his consistency and the rising popularity of Javelin in India.

questions.question: Identify this iconic trophy awarded to the winners of the FIFA World Cup.
questions.explanation: The current trophy has been used since 1974, replacing the Jules Rimet Trophy.
questions.fact: It is made of 18-carat gold and depicts two human figures holding up the Earth.
questions.expected_discussion: Explain the history of the Jules Rimet trophy and its theft.

questions.question: What are these symbols which are the hallmark of the Olympic movement?
questions.explanation: The five interlaced rings symbolize the union of the five continents.
questions.fact: The symbol was designed in 1912 by Pierre de Coubertin, the founder of the modern Olympic Games.
questions.expected_discussion: Point out that the rings are interlaced to show connection.

questions.question: Name this stadium in Qatar which hosted the final match of the 2022 FIFA World Cup.
questions.explanation: Lusail Stadium is the largest stadium in Qatar and hosted ten matches during the 2022 World Cup, including the final.
questions.fact: The stadium's design is inspired by the hand-crafted bowls found throughout the Arab and Islamic world.
questions.expected_discussion: Discuss the architectural inspiration of the stadium.

questions.question: Identify this Indian badminton player who is the first Indian to win two individual Olympic medals.
questions.explanation: Sindhu won Silver at Rio 2016 and Bronze at Tokyo 2020.
questions.fact: She was also the first Indian to become the Badminton World Champion in 2019.
questions.expected_discussion: Highlight her big-match temperament in major tournaments.

questions.question: Identify the athlete who holds the world record for 100m sprint, often seen in clips like this.
questions.explanation: Usain Bolt set the world record of 9.58 seconds at the 2009 World Championships.
questions.fact: He is an 8-time Olympic gold medalist and the only sprinter to win Olympic 100m and 200m titles at three consecutive Olympics (2008, 2012, 2016).
questions.expected_discussion: Discuss his charisma and the 'Lightning Bolt' pose.

questions.question: Which sport is shown in this clip, where athletes throw a spear-like object?
questions.explanation: Javelin throw is a track and field event where the javelin, a spear about 2.5m in length, is thrown.
questions.fact: The modern javelin throw is part of the Olympic decathlon and heptathlon.
questions.expected_discussion: Explain the technical nuances like the run-up and release angle.

questions.question: In football, if a commentator says 'The penalty is being taken from 10 yards out', what is the mistake?
questions.answer: The penalty spot is actually 12 yards from the goal line
questions.explanation: The penalty spot is officially 12 yards (11 meters) from the center of the goal line.
questions.fact: Penalty kicks were first introduced to the laws of the game in 1891.
questions.expected_discussion: Ask students if they know other common football measurements.

questions.question: The Paris 2024 Opening Ceremony was unique for being held on which famous river?
questions.explanation: Paris 2024 was the first Summer Olympics to have its opening ceremony outside of a stadium.
questions.fact: Over 10,000 athletes paraded on boats along a 6-kilometer route on the river.
questions.expected_discussion: Discuss the challenges of security and weather for such an event.

questions.question: Which football superstar is famous for the 'Siu' celebration shown in many clips?
questions.explanation: Cristiano Ronaldo is the all-time leading goalscorer in international football.
questions.fact: The 'Siu' celebration involves a mid-air pirouette and landing in a power pose while shouting 'Siu!'
questions.expected_discussion: Talk about his fitness and longevity in professional football.

questions.question: Who was the first Indian to win an individual Gold medal at the Olympic Games?
questions.explanation: Abhinav Bindra won the gold in the Men's 10m Air Rifle event at the 2008 Beijing Olympics.
questions.fact: It was India's first-ever individual gold medal and the first gold since the men's hockey team won in 1980.
questions.expected_discussion: Describe the precision required in shooting sports.

questions.question: Which country has won the most FIFA World Cup titles in history?
questions.explanation: Brazil has won the FIFA World Cup five times (1958, 1962, 1970, 1994, 2002).
questions.fact: Brazil is also the only nation to have played in every World Cup tournament.
questions.expected_discussion: Mention famous Brazilian players like Pelé and Ronaldo.

questions.question: What does the abbreviation VAR stand for in the context of football refereeing?
questions.explanation: VAR is used to review decisions made by the head referee with the use of video footage.
questions.fact: It was first written into the Laws of the Game by the IFAB in 2018.
questions.expected_discussion: Discuss the controversies and benefits of technology in sports.

questions.question: In which city were the first modern Olympic Games held in 1896?
questions.explanation: The 1896 Summer Olympics were held in Athens, Greece, as a tribute to the ancient Olympic Games.
questions.fact: Only 14 nations participated in the first modern Olympics, with a total of 43 events.
questions.expected_discussion: Contrast the size of 1896 Games with the scale of modern Olympics.

questions.question: Arrange these FIFA World Cup winners in order from the most recent to the oldest: Germany, France, Argentina, Spain.
questions.explanation: The winners were Spain in 2010, Germany in 2014, France in 2018, and Argentina in 2022.
questions.fact: This decade saw four different winners from two different continents (Europe and South America).
questions.expected_discussion: Note that all these winners are either from Europe or South America.

questions.question: How long is a standard football match in minutes, excluding stoppage time?
questions.explanation: A match consists of two halves of 45 minutes each.
questions.fact: The duration was first established in 1866.
questions.expected_discussion: Mention the introduction of 'stoppage time' to compensate for delays.

questions.question: Which major tennis tournament is played on grass courts in London?
questions.explanation: Wimbledon is the oldest tennis tournament in the world and the only Grand Slam played on grass.
questions.fact: Players must follow a strict white-only dress code.
questions.expected_discussion: Talk about the unique tradition of strawberries and cream at Wimbledon.

questions.question: How many total medals did India win at the Paris 2024 Olympics?
questions.explanation: India won 1 Silver (Neeraj Chopra) and 5 Bronze medals.
questions.fact: Manu Bhaker became the first Indian athlete in independent India to win two medals in a single Olympic edition.
questions.expected_discussion: Discuss Manu Bhaker's historic achievement in shooting.

questions.question: Who is known as the 'Flying Sikh' of India?
questions.explanation: Milkha Singh was an Indian track and field sprinter who won four Asian Games gold medals.
questions.fact: He narrowly missed an Olympic medal, finishing fourth in the 400m final at the 1960 Rome Olympics.
questions.expected_discussion: Reminisce about the movie 'Bhaag Milkha Bhaag' based on his life.

questions.question: What color card does a referee show to send a player off the field in football?
questions.explanation: A red card signifies that a player has been dismissed from the match.
questions.fact: The red and yellow card system was introduced in the 1970 World Cup.
questions.expected_discussion: Explain the difference between a direct red card and two yellow cards.
